column1: # check-all.sh baseline — CCPR's own expected exit code per shipped check.
# Format: <name>\t<expected-exit>\t<note>  (note is free text, for humans;
# check-all.sh never parses it). Comment lines (#) and blank lines are
# ignored. Tab-separated on purpose (readable and diffable without jq;
# bash 3.2 has no associative arrays, so `IFS=$'\t' read` is the parser).
# The note states the DURABLE REASON this exit code is the right
# expectation -- never what a run measured. A measurement here has no
# reader: nothing parses it, nothing re-derives it, nothing goes red when
# it is wrong. It is invalidated by the next commit (artifact-gate's file
# count went 313 -> 323 -> 328 -> 332 in three days), and where it
# described the maintainer's own machine -- targets present, deny-list
# entries, consumers configured -- it was simply false on any CI runner,
# which reports could-not-run for exactly those checks. What a run measured
# is in that run's own report, where it is current by definition.
# scripts/tests/test_check_all.py enforces the separation.
# A note may be EMPTY (two fields, no trailing tab) when a check has no
# reason to state beyond "exit 0 is the ordinary outcome". check-all.sh's
# reader takes that shape unchanged -- b_rest is a read target it never
# consumes.
# This file declares EXPECTATIONS, never commands — the check catalogue
# (name -> which script/args run it) lives once, in check-all.sh itself.
# ONE entry is non-zero BY DESIGN, not a regression: memory-lint.sh's
# long-standing memory-freshness warnings. It was two until 30.08.2026 --
# doc-volume-check.sh now scans only git-tracked files, so the oversized
# files it used to report (all of them untracked working state under
# docs/memory/) are out of its scope and its expected exit is 0.
# Three entries are environment-independent by construction rather than by
# luck: memory-lint and conformance-run report their own scope, so a
# machine without those targets gets could-not-run instead of a divergence,
# and doc-volume-check measures only what git tracks.
# Re-measure and update this file DELIBERATELY when a check's expected
# outcome actually changes -- the same "re-measure the pair together, never
# adjust one" discipline CONTRIBUTING.md already asks of the -t . /
# --without-t measurement (WI-0126 lineage). Do not let this file drift
# silently out of step with the tree it describes.
# No provenance line here on purpose. "Measured on HEAD <sha>" is itself a
# freshness claim, and an unchecked one goes stale exactly like the counts
# it vouches for -- the line this replaces named a HEAD three commits older
# than one of its values and five older than another, in a header that asks
# for deliberate re-measurement. With the measurements gone, nothing left
# in this file is bound to a point in time.
